Deluge in Limpopo Final Script Tx Sunday 25th Jan 2026 Video

Thunder and music and on screen text

Limpopo Province: January 2026

Up sound Pilot
Uh we are going to look at the damage on the R40. Apparently there’s a segment of the road that was completely washed away.

Thierry Boulanger ( spell checked)
There were so many forecasts saying its not going to rain and others saying its going to rain

V0 1
A farm watch in Hoedspruit, Limpopo, keeps a close eye on forecasts from the SA Weather Service

Thierry Boulanger
It started off with level three warnings, then we saw the first level 5 coming up

VO 2
Kruger National Park’s disaster team assembles, and as the weather intensifies, guests and staff begin evacuating

Reynold Thakhuli KNP GM, Media
So early warning systems really, really assisted us,

Kruger airlifting people

VO 3 fact checked camps
In the storm’s aftermath, no fatalities are reported in the park, but 15 camps remain closed and more than 40 % of revenue is being lost

The popular Letaba camp is under water, and so is the staff accommodation at Shingwedzi

Music sequence dramatic visuals

VO 4
Elsewhere in places like Giyani and into Mpumalanga the rain wreaks havoc.

Music up sound

Close to 40 lives are lost and a national disaster is declared.

UP sound

And as the week comes to an end, the rain keeps falling.

Thierry Boulanger Chairperson: Hoedspruit Farm Watch

Some of the places had about 996 ml of rain. That’s a metre of water

VO 5
Communities cut off, roads and bridges washed away

Up Sound
Do not attempt this at all!

VO 6
Lives are lost, while others narrowly escape

FADE TO BLACK

Up sound weather service
A very serious and historic red level ten warning has been issued by the weather service

VO 7
With more bad weather predicted, our producer and cameraman head to Limpopo by car… unsure if the roads are open

Joy up sound
Well when they said rain ….they weren’t kidding

VO 8 ( not all flights were cancelled hence “my”
The plan is for me to fly in later …but my commercial flight is cancelled

Joy up Sound
“ We have no presenter here to bring this story to you, so you just have / me the producer and Willem

V0 9
The storms impact is immediate: within days 439 roads are damaged, with around 600km urgently needing repair

Joy Up
Oh damn, now what do we do?

VO 10
A bridge straddling the Makhutswi River which flows into the Olifants, is one of the many damaged in the province

Riaan Van Aswegen
I think we are over the 2000 floodline here

VO 11
Riaan Van Aswegen is a local resident

Riaan Van Aswegen
If you look at the debris and all the damage on that bridge the water must have gone over 2 metres over this bridge and where it is now its about 6- 7 metres down – so this river rose about 7 metres to get to this level and do all this damage

VO 12
The Oliphants river, lined with popular tourist lodges, became a raging torrent, as flood waters built up behind the sluice gates upstream.

Up sound pilot
There’s four open on the whole thing.

Brenda Du Plessis and her husband Leon, own this lodge and safari business

up sound of water roaring

Brenda says Leon pleaded with the local water board to open the sluices but he was turned away.

Brenda Du Plessis
He barely made it, then it hit him: there is a massive amount of water. We need to get out!

VO 13
The family, staff and a guest tried to evacuate


Brenda
We didn’t know if we would make it, because the nearby mine, had blocked our way out

VO 14
As the waters rose, their vehicle got stuck, forcing all 18 of them to walk to safety in the dark and rain to await rescue

Brenda
I managed to call my daughter Tanya to tell her we're underwater- call Deidre. And then the signal went dead.
Joy
You must have been terrified Brenda
Brenda
Terribly. Terribly. We didn’t think we would make it.
Tanya
My moms last words were Tanya send help. We are underwater
Joy
Did you think you would see them again?
Tanya
No. I didn’t think I would see them again.

VO 15
The airforce was called in by Farmers organisation AgriLimpopo and all 18 people were airlifted to safety… at night in the driving rain

Tanya
I can still see it clearly - I ran to them the moment their car pulled in and I just hugged them.
Brenda
It’s a feeling you can't even begin to describe. I just said thank you God! Thank you God, for showing mercy to each and every one of us.

VO 16
Later, our crew sees the devastation around the Du Plessis lodge from the air. The pilots assisting the rescue and emergency supply effort have shown remarkable courage

Marlon Lewinsky
And now the lightning has started -I am just wondering if we shouldn't give it ten minutes and see which way it's moving.


VO 17
Marlon Lewinsky is with the Bateleurs, a wildlife and conservation NGO of volunteer Pilots

Marlon up sound
I am looking at that storm, it's getting quite dark there.

VO 18
Joy and Willem join Marlon as he tracks along the Olifants, seeing for the first time the extent of this natural catastrophe.

Below is the lodge.

Joy Up sound
Ya that is destruction.
Marlon
It's been a bitter sweet flight, interesting, but sad at the same time

Gerry takes off

Thierry Boulanger
These pilots are heroes.

VO 19
Thierry Boulanger is chairperson of the Hoedspruit Farm Watch

Thierry
The fact they flew in these conditions … the amount of casavacs they have done so far. I heard these choppers running day and night

Chopper take off

VO 20
Donovan De Wet has been flying almost non- stop. In a matter of days, he’s airlifted over 60 people to safety. When not saving lives, he’s delivered anything from eggs to generators to those stranded in the greater Kruger

Capt. Donovan De Wet: Bastion Aviation
I have seen swimming pools washed into the river, decking hanging on the side of the river. To see the extent of the damage… one property had 17 vehicles stuck all in a row
VO 21
While not stuck, our crew can’t get to a scheduled interview with the Black Mamba’s, an anti poaching unit with headquarters on the Olifants River

Leitah Mkhabela Supervisor Black Mambas
Morning Everyone this is how our road looks, from our compound…

VO 22
Their access road had collapsed

But our crew bumps into some of their members trying to get home…

Joy Summers up sound
For reasons I can't really understand we are doing a bit of a transfer here/ we are filling up but this isn't all that is coming

VO 23
And they have unusual company: a goat being taken to safety rather than being left to fend for itself against hungry predators.

Up sound Goat gets in and makes a racket!

It seems to have been washed down the river and the Mambas have come across it on patrol. Joy and Willem are convinced to contribute to the rescue mission.

Up sound driving

With infrastructure collapsing the Hoedspruit farm watch has sprung into action

up sound

Correct strap Lafras Tremper: Head of Operations, Hoedspruit Farm Watch

VO 24
Lafras Tremper heads the reaction unit

His team has often been in the swollen rivers saving lives



Lafras Tremper
There were a lot of vehicles, Hilux bakkies, Fortuna’s - all washed off the road. Two of the vehicles are still missing, we couldn't find them, but luckily, we managed to rescue everyone. We used long lines, ropes tied together, we pulled people out of the water.

VO25
This is the Zand River bridge on the outskirts of Hoedspruit. It’s normally a drive riverbed

Lavras
Where I am standing the water was up to here so right up to the 60 sign was under water. The biggest problem is many people take chances and then the vehicles are washed away

VO 26
They closed the bridge and volunteers spent a waterlogged night with crocodiles and hippos to prevent any fatalities

Lafras
It was a mad evening.

Thierry Boulanger
When they were keeping the bridge closed, the hippos pitched up. That is what the lowveld is all about

VO 27
But they’re not just closing bridges, they’re rebuilding them.

Lafras Tremper
I got on the radio group and said we need help. Women arrived with food, men came to braai for us. We had TLB’s. So that night around 6 30 pm, the road was open again.

VO 28
So strong was this river, that it washed away an entire bridge. Almost claiming the life of Pinky Mkhonto

Lavras Tremper
We managed to rescue her, she’s in the hospital at the moment


VO 29
Told to evacuate from work, her usual path out was flooded and she fell.

Pinky Mkhonto
I was deep underwater and I was dragged for quite a distance. The people I was with couldn't help me.

VO 30
For 30 minutes Pinky fought for her life, but she was drowning.

Pinky Mkhonto
It was an out of body experience while deep in the water, eventually I was trapped by a rock, and that is when I heard a man’s voice asking me to reach out for his hand. I did and he pulled me out.

VO 31
Pinky is one of the lucky ones. More than 40 people are now confirmed dead in the floods.

That number is likely to rise as rescuers and other workers make their way through the debris.

The Kruger Park is pleading for assistance, saying it can’t rebuild on its own. And, throughout all of it, a nagging feeling that this may be the new normal.

THE END

PROMO ONE
VO 1
Houses washed away, people in peril and lives saved in the nick of time
Tanya
My moms last words were Tanya send help. We are underwater
Joy
Did you think you would see them again?
Tanya
No. I didn’t think I would see them again.
VO
A national disaster is declared as floodwaters decimate the North East of the country


PROMO TWO
VO
The Kruger National Park is calling for help to rebuild after floods destroyed roads, bridges and camps.

Reynold Thakhuli KNP GM
So early warning systems really, really assisted us,

VO
Camps closed, revenue down… and a difficult future ahead.

PROMO THREE
Donovan De Wet Bastion Aviation
We didn't sleep well at night

VO
As floods swept Limpopo, pilots answered the call.

Thierry
These pilots are heroes. I heard these choppers running day and night

VO
And farmers saved lives on the ground

Lafras Tremper
I got on the radio group and said we need help. Women arrived with food, / We had TLB’s. So that night around 6 30 pm, the road was open again.

Thierry Boulanger When they were keeping the bridge closed, the hippos pitched up. That is what the lowveld is all about VO 27 But they’re not just closing bridges, they’re rebuilding them. Lafras Tremper I got on the radio group and said we need help. Women arrived with food, men came to braai for us. We had TLB’s. So that night around 6 30 pm, the road was open again. VO 28 So strong was this river, that it washed away an entire bridge. Almost claiming the life of Pinky Mkhonto Lavras Tremper We managed to rescue her, she’s in the hospital at the moment VO 29 Told to evacuate from work, her usual path out was flooded and she fell. Pinky Mkhonto I was deep underwater and I was dragged for quite a distance. The people I was with couldn't help me. VO 30 For 30 minutes Pinky fought for her life, but she was drowning. Pinky Mkhonto It was an out of body experience while deep in the water, eventually I was trapped by a rock, and that is when I heard a man’s voice asking me to reach out for his hand. I did and he pulled me out. VO 31 Pinky is one of the lucky ones. More than 40 people are now confirmed dead in the floods. That number is likely to rise as rescuers and other workers make their way through the debris. The Kruger Park is pleading for assistance, saying it can’t rebuild on its own. And, throughout all of it, a nagging feeling that this may be the new normal.
